title: How do you travel from 9 back to 3 on the number line?
description: A walker goes from nine back to three along the number line and the steps are counted to the left. The journey is written as an addition and as a take away. Keeko's doubt is that the movement is positive six.
teaching_notes: One idea: a journey to the left on the number line is a negative movement, here negative six, and it matches three take away nine. Watch for students who count six and forget that the walker goes backward.

source: Now, from 9, if you wish to go to 3, how much must you trave
video_script.why: The child sees that a journey to the left on the number line is a negative movement, and that it matches target minus start.
video_script.substitution: The book's own number line, walking backward from nine to three.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book, with a walker going backward from nine to three
video_script.wrong_move: counts six steps but ignores that the walker goes backward, so writes the movement as positive
video_script.payoff_line: The journey from nine to three is six steps backward, which is negative six.

final_answer.spoken: six steps backward, a movement of negative six

maths_rules: stand on 9, walk left: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 is 6 steps backward
slip: 9 + 6 = 15, which is not 3; a movement of +6 from 9 goes forward to 15
video_script.design: A number line from 0 to 10 with a walker on 9; the steps are counted one at a time while the walker moves left.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 10 with a walker standing on 9 and 3 lit up

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the number line is drawn
marks.ask: the number 3 lights up and a question mark appears between them

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the number line.
<bookmark mark='walker'/>You stand on nine and wish to go to three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much must you travel along the line?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: right = forward = positive;  left = backward = negative

marks.right: an arrow to the right is marked forward, positive
marks.left: an arrow to the left is marked backward, negative

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>On the number line, going to the right is forward, and that is positive.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Going to the left is backward, and that is negative.

marks.given: the start and the target are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the starting number is nine, and the target number is three.

marks.find: the words movement needed are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the movement needed.

beats.on_screen: walker steps 9 to 8 to 7 to 6 to 5 to 4 to 3; step count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 to the left

marks.walk: the walker steps left from 9 through 8, 7, 6, 5 and 4 to 3, and the count 1 to 6 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='walk'/>Step one, walk to the left from nine, and count the steps.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Eight, seven, six, five, four and three make six steps.

marks.dir: the six steps are coloured as backward steps

narration: <bookmark mark='dir'/>Step two, the steps are backward, so the movement is negative six.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Starting number plus movement is the target number, so nine plus negative six is three.

marks.rule: the line Target number - Starting number = Movement is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, the same fact as a take away, target number take away starting number.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Three take away nine is negative six.

marks.ans: 6 steps backward, movement -6 is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The walker has made six steps in the backward direction.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The journey from nine to three is six steps backward, which is negative six.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 9 + 6 = 15 shown with the walker on 15, far from 3; the wrong sign struck out

marks.doubt: the movement with a plus sign is written
marks.short: 9 + 6 = 15 is written and the walker jumps to 15
marks.fix: the plus sign is struck out and replaced by a minus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the movement is positive six, because there are six steps.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Nine plus positive six is fifteen, which is far from three.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The walker goes backward, so the six steps must be negative.
